question_html: How is a Bill of Exchange defined under commercial practice and law?

options.A: An instrument in writing containing a conditional promise signed by the debtor
options.B: An instrument in writing containing an unconditional order signed by the maker directing a certain person to pay a certain sum of money only to or to the order of a certain person or to the bearer
options.C: A bank note or currency note issued by the central bank
options.D: A verbal agreement to pay money on demand

answer_html: Answer: (B) A Bill of Exchange is defined as an instrument in writing containing an unconditional order signed by the maker directing a certain person to pay a certain sum of money only to or to the order of a certain person or to the bearer of the instrument[cite: 16].
topic_text: Meaning and Characteristics of Bills of Exchange

question_html: Which of the following parties are involved in a Promissory Note?
answer_html: Answer: (B) There are 2 parties (Maker and Payee) in a promissory note, whereas there are generally 3 parties in a bill of exchange[cite: 16].

question_html: Under Section 31(2) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, a promissory note CANNOT be made payable to whom?

options.B: The order of a specific person

answer_html: Answer: (C) Under Section 31(2) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, a promissory note cannot be made payable to bearer[cite: 16].

question_html: How many days of grace are added to the due date of a bill of exchange payable otherwise than on demand to arrive at the maturity date?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Every instrument payable otherwise than on demand is entitled to three days of grace[cite: 16].
topic_text: Days of Grace and Maturity Date

question_html: What is the due date when the calculated maturity date of a bill falls on a public holiday?
answer_html: Answer: (C) When the due date is a public holiday, the preceding business day will be the due date[cite: 16].
topic_text: Calculation of Due Date on Public Holiday

question_html: What is the due date when the calculated maturity date falls on an emergency or unforeseen holiday?
answer_html: Answer: (B) When the due date is an emergency/unforeseen holiday, the next following day will be the due date[cite: 16].
topic_text: Calculation of Due Date on Emergency Holiday

question_html: What are the fees charged by a Notary Public for officially noting the fact and reasons of dishonour of a bill called?
answer_html: Answer: (C) The fee charged by a Notary Public for noting the fact of dishonour with reasons is known as noting charges[cite: 16].

question_html: When an acceptor pays a bill of exchange before its maturity date and receives a rebate or discount for premature payment, how is that rebate treated by the acceptor?
answer_html: Answer: (B) The rebate becomes the income of the acceptor and the expense of the payee[cite: 16].

question_html: What is a Bill of Exchange drawn in one country and made payable in another country called?
answer_html: Answer: (B) A foreign bill of exchange is one which is drawn in one country and is payable in another[cite: 16].

question_html: What are bills drawn and accepted exclusively to finance mutual fund requirements without actual underlying trade transactions called?
answer_html: Answer: (B) When bills are used to raise finance without underlying trade sales, they are known as accommodation bills[cite: 16].

question_html: When a bill is sent to the bank with instructions to retain it till maturity and realise it on that date without getting immediate credit, what is it called?
answer_html: Answer: (C) If the bill is sent to the bank with instructions to retain till maturity and realise, it is known as a bill sent for collection[cite: 16].

question_html: In the books of the drawee, the amount not ultimately paid due to insolvency should be credited to which account?
answer_html: Answer: (B) In the books of the drawee of the bill, the amount not ultimately paid due to insolvency should be credited to Deficiency Account[cite: 16].

question_html: What type of account is the 'Bills Payable Account' in the ledger?
answer_html: Answer: (C) The bills payable account is a personal account that represents a liability[cite: 16].

question_html: When does the term of a bill drawn 'after sight' commence?

options.A: From the date of drawing the bill
options.B: From the date of acceptance or sighting

answer_html: Answer: (B) The term of a bill after sight commences from the date of acceptance / sighting of the bill[cite: 16].

question_html: When does the term of a bill drawn 'after date' commence?

options.B: From the date of drawing the bill
options.C: From the date of receipt by payee

answer_html: Answer: (B) The term of a bill after date commences from the date of drawing of the bill[cite: 16].

question_html: On 1.1.2022, A draws a bill on B for ₹1,20,000 for 3 months. What will be the exact maturity date of the bill?
answer_html: Answer: (C) 3 months from 1st January is 1st April. Adding 3 days of grace gives 4th April 2022[cite: 16].

question_html: On 16.6.2022, P draws a bill on Q for ₹1,25,000 for 30 days. If 19th July is a public holiday, what will be the maturity date of the bill?
answer_html: Answer: (B) 30 days from 16th June: June has 30 days (14 days left in June) + 16 days in July = 16th July + 3 days of grace = 19th July. Since 19th July is a public holiday, the preceding business day (18th July) is the due date[cite: 16].

question_html: PQ draws a bill on XY for ₹1,30,000 on 1.1.2022. XY accepts it on 4.1.2022 for a period of 3 months after date. What is the maturity date?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Since it is a bill 'after date', the term starts from the date of drawing (1.1.2022). 3 months after 1st January plus 3 days of grace is 4.4.2022[cite: 16].

question_html: A bill of ₹1,20,000 was discounted by Saras with her banker for ₹1,18,800. At maturity, the bill was returned dishonoured, and noting charges were ₹200. How much amount will the bank deduct from Saras's bank balance at the time of dishonour?
answer_html: Answer: (C) The bank will deduct the full bill amount plus noting charges: $1,20,000 + 200 = \text{₹}1,20,200$[cite: 16].
topic_text: Dishonour of Discounted Bill with Noting Charges

question_html: X draws a bill on Y for ₹3,00,000 on 1.1.2022 for 3 months after sight. The date of acceptance is 6.1.2022. What will be the maturity date of the bill?
answer_html: Answer: (B) For a bill 'after sight', the term commences from the date of acceptance (6.1.2022). 3 months from 6th January is 6th April. Adding 3 days of grace gives 9.4.2022[cite: 16].

question_html: X sold goods to Y for ₹5,00,000. Y paid cash ₹4,30,000. X granted a 2% cash discount on the balance, and Y requested X to draw a bill for the remaining balance. What will be the amount of the bill?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Balance due before discount = $5,00,000 - 4,30,000 = \text{₹}70,000$. Discount = 2% of ₹70,000 = ₹1,400. Amount of bill = $70,000 - 1,400 = \text{₹}68,600$[cite: 16].
topic_text: Bill Amount Calculation after Trade/Cash Discount

question_html: On 1.1.2022, X draws a bill on Y for ₹5,00,000 for 3 months. X got the bill discounted on 4.1.2022 at 12% p.a. What is the amount of discount on the bill?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Discount = $5,00,000 \times (12/100) \times (3/12) = \text{₹}15,000$[cite: 16].

question_html: Mr. Jay draws a bill on Mr. John for ₹3,00,000 on 1.1.2022 for 3 months. On 4.2.2022, John got the bill discounted at 12% rate. What is the amount of discount?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Maturity date is 4.4.2022. Period from discounting (4.2.2022) to maturity (4.4.2022) is 2 months. Discount = $3,00,000 \times (12/100) \times (2/12) = \text{₹}6,000$[cite: 16].

question_html: XZ draws a bill on YZ for ₹2,00,000 for 3 months on 1.1.2022. The bill is discounted with banker at a charge of ₹1,000. At maturity the bill is returned dishonoured. In the books of XZ, for dishonour, by how much will the bank account be credited?
answer_html: Answer: (B) When a discounted bill is dishonoured, the bank deducts the full face value of the bill (₹2,00,000) from the drawer's account[cite: 16].
topic_text: Bank Credit on Dishonour of Discounted Bill

question_html: On 1.1.2022, XA draws a bill on YB for ₹1,00,000. At maturity YB requests XA to renew the bill for 2 months at 12% p.a. interest. What is the amount of interest payable?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Interest = $1,00,000 \times (12/100) \times (2/12) = \text{₹}2,000$[cite: 16].
topic_text: Interest Calculation on Renewal of Bill

question_html: On 1st January 2022, Ankita sells goods for ₹5,00,000 to Bhavika and draws a bill at 3 months. On 1st March 2022, Bhavika retires her acceptance under rebate of 12% per annum. What is the amount of rebate allowed?
answer_html: Answer: (B) The bill is retired 1 month before maturity (from 1 March to 4 April, roughly 1 month). Rebate = $5,00,000 \times (12/100) \times (1/12) = \text{₹}5,000$[cite: 16].

question_html: Rita owed ₹1,00,000 to Siriman. On 1st October 2021, Rita accepted a bill drawn by Siriman for 3 months. Siriman got it discounted for ₹99,000. On renewal, Rita paid ₹50,000 in cash, interest of ₹1,500, and accepted a new bill for the balance. What is the amount of the new bill?
answer_html: Answer: (A) The new bill is drawn for the unpaid principal balance of the original bill, which is ₹50,000 (interest is paid in cash)[cite: 16].

question_html: X draws on Y a bill of exchange for ₹30,000 on 1st April 2022 for 3 months. X discounts it for ₹28,800 and immediately remits ₹9,600 to Y. On due date, X accepts a new bill for ₹42,000. What was the total discount on the first bill?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Face value = ₹30,000, discounted proceeds = ₹28,800. Discount = $30,000 - 28,800 = \text{₹}1,200$[cite: 16].

question_html: On 1st January 2022, Vilas draws a bill of exchange for ₹10,000 due after 3 months on Eknath. Eknath retires the bill on 4th March 2022 at 12% p.a. discount. What is the amount of discount/interest in Eknath's books?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Maturity date is 4th April. Retirement on 4th March is exactly 1 month before maturity. Discount = $10,000 \times (12/100) \times (1/12) = \text{₹}100$[cite: 16].

question_html: Mr. David draws two bills on Mr. Thomas on 1.1.2022: ₹16,000 (2 months) and ₹10,000 (3 months). On 20.3.2022, Thomas retires the ₹10,000 bill with a discount rebate of ₹100. What amount is received by David on retirement?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Face value ₹10,000 less rebate of ₹100 = ₹9,900[cite: 16].
topic_text: Amount Received on Retirement of Bill

question_html: Who is the party that makes the order to pay in a Bill of Exchange?
answer_html: Answer: (B) The party which makes the order is known as the drawer[cite: 16].
topic_text: Parties to Bill of Exchange - Drawer

question_html: Who is the party that accepts the order to pay in a Bill of Exchange?
answer_html: Answer: (B) The party which accepts the order is known as the acceptor (drawee)[cite: 16].
topic_text: Parties to Bill of Exchange - Acceptor

question_html: Can a bill of exchange be accepted conditionally?

options.B: Yes, a bill of exchange can be accepted conditionally

answer_html: Answer: (B) A bill of exchange can be accepted conditionally, whereas a promissory note cannot be made conditionally[cite: 16].

question_html: Is notice of dishonour required in the case of a Promissory Note?

options.B: No, notice of dishonour is not required in case of promissory note

answer_html: Answer: (B) Notice of dishonour is not required in case of a promissory note[cite: 16].
topic_text: Notice of Dishonour for Promissory Note

question_html: What entry is passed by the payee when a Bill of Exchange or Promissory Note is received?

options.A: Debit Drawee, Credit Bills Receivable A/c
options.B: Debit Bills Receivable A/c, Credit Drawee/Maker A/c
options.C: Debit Bank A/c, Credit Bills Receivable A/c
options.D: Debit Sales A/c, Credit Bills Receivable A/c

answer_html: Answer: (B) Bills Receivable Account is debited and Drawee/Maker of the note is credited[cite: 16].
topic_text: Initial Entry on Receipt of Bill

question_html: A draws upon B three bills of exchange of ₹3,000, ₹2,000, and ₹1,000 respectively. The first bill of ₹3,000 is mutually cancelled, B paying 50% in cash and accepting a new bill for the balance plus ₹100 interest. What is the amount of the new bill accepted by B?
answer_html: Answer: (B) 50% of ₹3,000 is ₹1,500 paid in cash. Remaining unpaid balance is ₹1,500 plus interest of ₹100, giving a new bill amount of ₹1,600[cite: 16].
topic_text: Renewal and Partial Cash Payment Calculation

question_html: Mr. David draws two bills on Mr. Thomas on 1.1.2022: ₹26,000 (2 months) and ₹10,000 (3 months). On 4.3.2022, Thomas requests renewal of the first bill with 18% p.a. interest for 2 months. What is the amount of interest on the renewed bill?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Interest on ₹26,000 at 18% p.a. for 2 months = $26,000 \times (18/100) \times (2/12) = \text{₹}780$[cite: 16].

question_html: Thomas became insolvent after accepting a renewed bill of ₹6,180 (including ₹180 interest). If only 50 paise in a rupee could be recovered from his estate, what is the amount of bad debt written off in David's books?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total claim = ₹6,180. Recovery at 50% = ₹3,090. Bad debt = $6,180 - 3,090 = \text{₹}3,090$[cite: 16].
topic_text: Insolvency Recovery and Bad Debts Calculation

question_html: For mutual accommodation, X draws a 4-month bill on Y for ₹4,000 on 1st April 2022. X discounts it at 6% p.a. and remits 50% of the proceeds to Y. What is the amount of discount shared by Y?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Total discount = $4,000 \times (6/100) \times (4/12) = \text{₹}80$. Since Y receives 50% of proceeds, Y's share of discount is 50% of ₹80 = ₹40[cite: 16].

question_html: In an accommodation arrangement, X becomes insolvent after accepting a bill of ₹7,000 drawn by Y. If 25 paise in a rupee is received from X's estate, what is the deficiency amount credited by X in his own books?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Total liability = ₹7,000. Paid (25%) = ₹1,750. Balance credited to deficiency account = $7,000 - 1,750 = \text{₹}5,250$ (Note: in Illustration 11, Y's account entry has deficiency of ₹2,625 for a specific partial settlement, but general deficiency on the total unpaid balance of ₹7,000 is ₹5,250)[cite: 16].

question_html: What is a Promissory Note defined as?

options.A: An unconditional order to pay a certain sum
options.B: An instrument in writing containing an unconditional undertaking signed by the maker to pay a certain sum
options.C: A verbal promise made in front of witnesses
options.D: A bank cheque payable on demand

answer_html: Answer: (B) A promissory note is an instrument in writing containing an unconditional undertaking signed by the maker to pay a certain sum of money only to or to the order of a certain person[cite: 16].

question_html: Does a Promissory Note require acceptance by the payee or drawee?

options.B: No, it does not require any acceptance

answer_html: Answer: (B) A promissory note does not require any acceptance because the maker himself writes the document promising to pay[cite: 16].

question_html: What is the primary liability on a Bill of Exchange?
answer_html: Answer: (B) The primary liability on a bill of exchange is that of the acceptor[cite: 16].
topic_text: Primary Liability on Bill of Exchange

question_html: What are Bills Receivable and Bills Payable Books maintained for?

options.B: As journals (Day Books) to record details of bills receivable and payable in chronological order

answer_html: Answer: (B) Bills receivable and bills payable books are journals (Day Books) to record in chronological order the details of bills receivable and bills payable[cite: 16].

question_html: When a bill is endorsed to a third party, what account is credited in the books of the endorser?
answer_html: Answer: (B) When a bill is endorsed, the Bills Receivable Account is credited and the receiving party's account is debited[cite: 16].

question_html: James owes Don ₹3,200 and sends Don's own acceptance in favour of Ralph for ₹3,160 in full settlement. What is the discount/rebate recorded in Don's books?
answer_html: Answer: (A) The settlement of ₹3,200 debt with an acceptance of ₹3,160 gives a discount of $3,200 - 3,160 = \text{₹}40$[cite: 16].

question_html: Don meets his acceptance in favour of Singh for ₹4,500 by endorsing John's acceptance for ₹4,450 in full settlement. What amount of discount is credited in Don's books?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Liability of ₹4,500 is settled by endorsing a bill of ₹4,450, resulting in a discount of $4,500 - 4,450 = \text{₹}50$[cite: 16].

question_html: Ray's acceptance of ₹3,100.80 in favour of Don is retired one month before the due date at 6% p.a. interest. What is the discount/rebate amount?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Rebate = $3,100.80 \times (6/100) \times (1/12) = \text{₹}15.50$[cite: 16].

question_html: Which of the following instruments cannot be a time instrument because it is always payable on demand?
answer_html: Answer: (B) A cheque cannot be a time instrument because a cheque is always payable on demand[cite: 16].

question_html: What is the validity period of a cheque in India after which it becomes a 'Stale Cheque' if unpresented?
answer_html: Answer: (C) A cheque has validity of 90 days from its date after that it becomes void, normally termed as 'Stale Cheque'[cite: 16].
